_comment: Substrate-accounting diagnostic (2026-07-02 ledger), env-gated SWEG_FOCUS_FIRE, default OFF. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that tells a player which target to keep shooting at. Following the precedent of simulator.target_economics and simulator.focus_fire (both explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core wound-allocation wording the heuristic's 'already damaged' read is built from, and cites the real-world doctrine that motivates it: commit successive activations to finishing a target already hurt rather than spreading fire onto fresh ones. The diagnostic this term answers found the anti-Knight fire BUDGET is not the problem (every archetype can remove a Knight's wounds within a handful of rounds of concentrated fire) but that fire SCATTERS — 86 to 95 percent of shooting activations aimed at a Knight deal zero damage, and the small amount of damage that does land rarely repeats onto the same platform, so no Knight is ever finished. simulator.target_economics (built the same wave) fixed the PER-ACTIVATION half of this gap (never dump fire into a hull this weapon cannot wound); this term supplies the missing CROSS-ACTIVATION half (once a target has been hurt, keep hurting it) using nothing but the current-vs-starting health the Unit already tracks — 10e has no in-battle healing, so a below-starting-health reading is durable, monotonic proof that fire already landed, whether from this same army earlier this round or surviving over from a prior round.

simulator.focus_fire_completion.rule_name: Allocate Attack (10e Core Rules, damage) — cross-activation ranged target-priority piloting heuristic
simulator.focus_fire_completion.quoted_text: If the target unit contains a model that has already lost any wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase, the controlling player must allocate further attacks to that model until either it is destroyed, or all the attacks have been saved or resolved.
simulator.focus_fire_completion.trigger: SWEG_FOCUS_FIRE=1 (default off, byte-identical when unset). For every enemy unit in the acting model's candidate pool during the Shooting phase (both the squad split-fire planner Battle._plan_squad_fire and the per-model fallback picker in Battle._do_shoot), compare the candidate's current_health against its profile.health (starting health). A candidate below starting health, AND that this attacker's weapon can meaningfully wound at all this activation (simulator._ranged_expected_wounds > 0, the same can't-hurt-it screen simulator.target_economics uses), receives a bonus that scales with how much of its health it has already lost.
simulator.focus_fire_completion.effect: AI shooting target-selection heuristic. A candidate at full starting health receives no bonus (1.0x). A candidate that has already lost wounds receives a bonus rising toward 3.0x as it nears death, strongly preferring it over an equally-woundable fresh target of the same class in the picker's lowest-effective-health min() key — the cross-activation completion term that makes successive friendly activations converge on finishing the SAME already-wounded target instead of scattering fire across many fresh ones. This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted core wound-allocation wording (a model that has already lost wounds must keep absorbing damage before its unit-mates) is the closest real rule concept (mandatory continuation of damage onto an already-hurt model) the heuristic's target-level analogue draws its shape from; it does not alter any dice, roll, or damage value, it only changes which already-legal target the AI's shooting picker selects. Faithful and even-handed: it is CLASS-shaped (any candidate meeting the already-wounded-and-woundable test scores the same bonus), never a single pre-designated unit — following the batch lesson from the per-faction target-selection levers (Votann on-objective, Chaos Knights below-half) that a bias rewarding a CLASS of target helps, while the rejected T'au single-Spotted-target bias over-concentrated and dragged the metric via closed-matrix collateral. Composes multiplicatively with simulator.target_economics and the existing screen / synapse / transport / oath / class-bias chain rather than replacing any of it; the can't-hurt-it screen it reuses means SWEG_FOCUS_FIRE never scores an unkillable wounded target artificially high even when SWEG_TARGET_ECONOMICS itself is left off.

_target_priority_doctrine_reference: Real-play doctrine motivating this heuristic, presented as doctrine (not a rules citation) per the same disclosure pattern as the _target_priority_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/target_economics.json: competitive anti-Knight play concentrates successive activations onto ONE chosen Knight until it dies rather than spreading damage across several, because killing a Knight outright is a matter of crossing its wound threshold, not weapon capability. Sources: https://www.goonhammer.com/start-competing-imperial-knights/ (Goonhammer's Imperial Knights faction-focus guide, already cited by simulator.focus_fire and simulator.target_economics in this project for the same 'commit fire where it can register' doctrine) and https://www.tabletopbattles.com/10th-edition-competitive-faction-focus-chaos-knights/ (already cited in data/overrides.json's DESPOILER-GUN-BUILD note for this project's Chaos Knights gun-build sourcing). NOTE (honesty about verification): WebFetch on both URLs returned no retrievable page content in this session (likely JS-rendered pages), so the specific phrase 'killing them is not the challenge' could not be independently re-confirmed against live text this session; both domains are nonetheless real, already-vetted sources elsewhere in this codebase for Knights-matchup doctrine, and the doctrine paraphrased above is the same one the docs/PILOT_FINDINGS.md anti-Knight-strategy research (workflow anti-knight-research, sourced Goonhammer/Wahapedia/tabletopbattles) already recorded and acted on: 'absolute focus-fire on one Knight' as the shared real-playbook tactic across Astra Militarum, Chaos Knights and Leagues of Votann matchups vs Imperial Knights.
